note: Per-claim evidence layer, v1 (September 2026). Each factual claim in a gap's dossier is listed with its sources, a status and a last-verified date. Statuses: verified (checked against the cited source), reported (attributed to a named organisation's publication), estimate (a modelled or approximate figure, labelled as such), source-to-confirm (stated in the dossier with primary attribution pending, queued for the next review pass). The prose dossier stays the reading layer; this is the audit layer. Coverage grows tier by tier, build-now entries first. Method kin: Discourse Graphs.

claims.claim: From April 2026, around 379 Pride in Place neighbourhood boards begin spending up to £20m each.
The 2026 Act obliges councils to establish neighbourhood governance arrangements.
Local Trust winds down in 2026; its Community Leadership Academy supported leaders across 150 Big Local areas and helped mobilise more than 6,000 first-time volunteers.
The government's community organiser training programmes ended years ago.
JRF has flagged capacity as the Pride in Place programme's key risk.
No body is charged with training, peer networks or governance support for the incoming resident decision-makers.
claims.note: An absence claim, checked by search during the July 2026 research pass.

claims.claim: mySociety runs TheyWorkForYou, WhatDoTheyKnow and FixMyStreet, cross-subsidised through consultancy and short grants.
Democracy Club crowd-sources candidate and results data the state does not publish, and the Electoral Commission is absorbing only the polling-station finder.
mySociety's Shifting Landscapes report of January 2026 concludes there is no systematic support for public-interest technology in the UK.
Careful Industries reaches the same conclusion about the absence of systematic support.
Germany's Sovereign Tech Fund pays for maintenance of critical open infrastructure.
claims.note: The fund's own publications are cited on gap 13; the cross-reference should be added here directly. Queued for the October 2026 review pass.

claims.claim: Grant funders prefer novelty over maintenance, leaving load-bearing civic services one funding cycle from shutdown.
Citizens UK has 19 chapters and over 100 staff, funded by member dues, project grants and a Lottery Solidarity Fund award of about £5m over nine years.
ACORN's dues-funded model sustains branches in around ten cities.
The state's Community Organisers Programme trained 500 organisers between 2011 and 2015 and ended without succession.
Foundations fund organising mainly through short project grants that conflict with the model's need for patient core money.
No UK equivalent exists of the dedicated organising philanthropy intermediaries of the US.
claims.note: The Civic Power Fund is the nascent UK exception; the claim holds at US scale and the wording needs sharpening at the October 2026 review.

claims.claim: The EU's Next Generation Internet initiative distributed around €140m to more than 1,200 projects in small cascade grants, largely through NLnet.
The Commission dropped NGI from the Horizon Europe 2025 work programme.
UK civil-society funders treat technology as unfundable infrastructure, and the Nesta and National Lottery digital funds have closed.
No domestic substitute exists at the €5k to €50k grant size where most independent maintainers live.
claims.note: An absence claim, checked by search during the July 2026 research pass.

claims.claim: GOV.UK Notify serves more than 1,500 public services and explicitly excludes charities, community pharmacies, hospices, housing associations and universities.
Notify's code is open source.
claims.note: True and easily shown; the alphagov repository should be cited directly. Queued for the October 2026 review pass.

claims.claim: Charities re-buy messaging, forms and payments at retail SaaS prices with donated funds.
No UK body provides equivalent shared digital infrastructure to civil society.
claims.note: An absence claim, checked by search during the July 2026 research pass.

claims.claim: The EU Cyber Resilience Act creates obligations for manufacturers and an open-source-software-steward category, phasing in through 2026-27.
UK-based foundations, SMEs and maintainers whose software reaches the EU market must comply regardless of Brexit.
The UK's Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, at report stage in June 2026, focuses on NIS-regulated sectors and makes no provision for open source stewardship.
claims.note: The stewardship point is an absence claim, verified by reading the bill documents for such provision and finding none.

claims.claim: No UK-facing CRA compliance help for maintainers exists.
claims.note: An absence claim, checked by search during the July 2026 research pass.

claims.claim: The British Youth Council, the UK's youth-led representative umbrella since 1948, went insolvent in March 2024 when its backer entered administration.
DCMS moved Youth Parliament delivery to the National Youth Agency as a government-contracted arrangement.
BYC's federating, Youth Select Committee and European Youth Forum representation functions have no successor.
claims.note: An absence claim, checked during the July 2026 research pass.

claims.claim: The UK is now one of very few European democracies without an independent national youth council.
claims.note: A comparative claim; the European Youth Forum's membership list is the checkable source to cite. Queued for the October 2026 review pass.

claims.claim: The National Citizen Service closed in March 2025 after over £1bn spent since 2011, cutting funding to around 250 delivery organisations.
The replacement programmes are place-based provision for disadvantaged areas rather than a universal mixing-and-service experience.
NCVO's Time Well Spent research shows youth-relevant participation roughly halving since 2018.
France runs the SNU and the US runs AmeriCorps, and the UK now has no national civic service pathway.
claims.note: The comparative half needs direct citations to the SNU and AmeriCorps programmes; the UK absence was checked in July 2026. Queued for the October review pass.

claims.claim: The Centre for Social Justice's Lost Boys work documents male NEET numbers up 40 per cent since the pandemic, against 7 per cent for women.
Suicide is the leading cause of death for young men aged 15 to 19.
claims.note: Cited via CSJ, which draws on official mortality statistics; the direct ONS citation should be added at the October 2026 review.

claims.claim: John Smith Centre polling finds young men markedly more right-leaning and distrustful than young women.
No UK funder runs a dedicated programme for young men's civic participation, while Rosa and the Tampon Tax legacy funds exist for women and girls.
claims.note: An absence claim, checked by search during the July 2026 research pass.

claims.claim: 61.5 per cent of young people get political information mainly from social media, and 73 per cent signed a petition or advocated online in the past year.
The Electoral Commission's Welcome to Your Vote Week is a school-focused education programme.
Party youth wings are actively recruiting, with Reform launching a student wing and the Conservatives relaunching theirs.
No at-scale nonpartisan registration-and-turnout operation exists in the UK.
claims.note: An absence claim, checked by search during the July 2026 research pass.

claims.claim: The Scouts' waiting list passed 100,000 in 2024.
claims.note: Currently cited to an encyclopedia entry; the Scout Association's own annual report is the primary source to substitute. Queued for the October 2026 review pass.

claims.claim: Girlguiding and the Scouts run joint growth projects, and both face adult-volunteer constraints.
Overall volunteering has declined since the pandemic.
No national mechanism recruits, trains or gives employer time-off entitlements to adult volunteers for youth movements.
claims.note: An absence claim, checked by search during the July 2026 research pass.

claims.claim: HS2 Phase 1 costs about £396m per mile against about £46m for comparable French high-speed lines, and Britain Remade's dataset of 138 transit and 104 road projects across 14 countries shows UK costs running two to eight times EU peers.
The Lower Thames Crossing consent alone cost about £300m.
NISTA's pipeline portal lists projects and values rather than standardised outturn unit costs, and the pipeline is worth £718bn.
Under the May 2025 Mansion House Accord, seventeen providers pledged 10 per cent of DC default funds to private markets by 2030, with 5 per cent in the UK.
claims.note: Recapped in the cited legal analysis; the Accord's own text is the primary source to add at the October 2026 review.

claims.claim: The Pension Schemes Act 2026 holds a backstop mandation power exercisable once between 2028 and 2032.
The British Growth Partnership's first fund closed at £200m, with Aegon UK, NatWest Cushon and M&G participating.
Few long-term asset funds offer UK venture or growth exposure at institutional scale.
claims.note: A market-scan assessment from the July 2026 research pass.

claims.claim: The Public Authorities (Fraud, Error and Recovery) Act 2025 lets DWP require banks to scan benefit claimants' accounts through Eligibility Verification Notices.
Rollout begins in 2026 on a test-and-learn basis.
The codes of practice governing the powers were finalised in May 2026.
The Information Commissioner raised concerns about the eligibility verification measure during the Bill's passage.
Neither the Act's review mechanisms nor the codes of practice require independent publication of error and false-positive rates.
claims.note: An absence claim: verified by reading the cited documents for such a requirement and finding none.

claims.claim: Roughly ten million accounts fall within the scope of the screening.
claims.note: A widely cited civil-society estimate of accounts in scope. Primary attribution is pending and queued for the October 2026 review pass.

claims.claim: DWP has documented bias problems in its fraud models.
claims.note: Refers to DWP's own machine-learning fairness disclosures as reported at the time. The primary disclosure document needs citing directly; queued for the October 2026 review pass.

claims.claim: No independent body or civil-society observatory monitors notice volumes or outcomes, and JUSTICE's published analysis covered the Bill rather than the rollout.
claims.note: An absence claim, checked by search during the July 2026 research pass; the JUSTICE briefing is cited as the sector's closest published work.
